headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared artifact handling; no direct write-conflict or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can pass artifacts and parameters, and LlamaFactory is an agent/LLM tool; if the pair is wired so LlamaFactory consumes Argo-produced content, prompt injection is plausible through shared artifacts. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Argo Workflows artifacts or parameters are fed into LlamaFactory prompts without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF the two systems are connected by a shared workspace or API bridge, attacker-controlled content can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Add a strict prompt/content sanitizer before LlamaFactory ingestion.
Require provenance labels on all Argo-produced artifacts.
Use a denylist for instruction-like tokens in transferred text.
Review one representative workflow for untrusted text flow.
requires-engineering: insert an isolation layer between workflow outputs and model prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters, but LlamaFactory has network egress none and no filesystem or clipboard surfaces, so the pair does not show a default exfiltration path. A leak would require an unusual integration not present in the profiles.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is manually mounted into LlamaFactory, artifact contents could be exposed.
IF an operator copies Argo outputs into LlamaFactory inputs, sensitive parameters may be revealed.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid mounting artifact directories into LlamaFactory.
Redact sensitive parameters before transfer.
Check that no outbound connector is enabled on LlamaFactory.
Document a manual handoff procedure for any shared files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows exposes REST/GRPC APIs and allowlisted egress, while LlamaFactory has no filesystem write, no git modification, no subprocesses, and no network egress. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable write surfaces, so a capability conflict is not plausible by default.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk would change.
IF additional permissions are added beyond the profiles, reassess for shared mutable state.
mitigations: Keep LlamaFactory read-only.
Do not grant shared filesystem write access.
Avoid shared git working trees.
Review any orchestrator permissions before deployment.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo Workflows can generate artifacts and parameters that LlamaFactory may consume as model inputs; if those outputs are treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream model behavior. The pair lacks a documented verification step, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory uses Argo outputs as training or prompt data without validation, errors can propagate.
IF Argo-produced artifacts are rendered or summarized by LlamaFactory, factual mistakes may be amplified.
mitigations: Add a validation step before LlamaFactory ingests Argo outputs.
Require human review for high-impact artifacts.
Separate raw data from model-facing text.
Log source provenance for each transferred artifact.
requires-engineering: implement schema checks on workflow outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is evidenced in either profile. Both agents are open-source with docs-only evidence, and neither profile shows PHI handling or a jurisdictional constraint, so a compliance breach is not supported.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into the pair, reassess compliance.
IF deployment policies impose residency or retention constraints, verify them separately.
mitigations: Confirm the data classes in scope.
Check retention settings in the deployment environment.
Avoid routing regulated data through the pair.
Record any jurisdictional requirements before rollout.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement if regulated data is expected.
